newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit stays in tight range, ends lower vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit stays in tight range, ends lower vs dollar.

text.p: The ringgit was trapped in a tight 10-point trading range against the dollar throughout Friday's session, closing lower after some positions adjustment in the morning, dealers said.

"There was nothing much happening in the market as most players are waiting for the (U.S.) jobs data," said a dealer with a local bank. "There is some pressure on the ringgit but strong support is expected at 2.50."
Dealers said though the U.S. jobs data, due at 1230 GMT, was not expected to have much impact, investors were not taking chances by keeping their commitments low.
There were no fresh leads to steer dollar/ringgit direction, they said.
Dealers said activity was more focused on ringgit/Singapore dollar cross trade.
At the local 1000 GMT close, the ringgit was at 2.4981/84 per dollar against 2.4962/72 on Thursday.
On the money market, most interbank rates retained their recent gains as the market remained tight and bids from finance companies were strong, dealers said.
The overnight rate, however, eased to 8.00 percent from 8.50 percent previously. -- Syed Azman (603-230 8911)
